PROTOCOL TITLE: A Phase II, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study of
Investigational Agent XJ-401 in Adult Patients with Relapsed/Refractory
Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma

PROTOCOL NUMBER: XJ401-201
VERSION: 3.0, dated 2026-06-01

1. BACKGROUND AND RATIONALE
Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL) remains a significant unmet medical need for patients
who relapse after standard chemoimmunotherapy. XJ-401 is a first-in-class
bispecific antibody targeting CD20 and CD3.

2. STUDY OBJECTIVES
Primary: Evaluate overall response rate (ORR) per Lugano criteria.
Secondary: Progression-free survival, duration of response, safety and
tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and patient-reported outcomes (PROs) via the
FACT-Lym questionnaire administered at baseline, cycle 3, cycle 6, and end of
treatment.

3. STUDY DESIGN
This is a multi-center, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled
trial across approximately 40 sites in North America and Europe. Patients will
be stratified by prior lines of therapy and lymphoma subtype.

4. ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA
Inclusion: Age >= 18 years; histologically confirmed NHL; ECOG performance
status 0-2; measurable disease per Lugano criteria; adequate organ function
(ANC >= 1000/uL, platelets >= 75,000/uL, creatinine clearance >= 40 mL/min,
AST/ALT <= 2.5x ULN, total bilirubin <= 1.5x ULN).
Exclusion: Active CNS lymphoma; prior CAR-T therapy within 3 months; active
autoimmune disease requiring systemic immunosuppression; known HIV, active
hepatitis B or C; pregnancy or breastfeeding.

5. STUDY PROCEDURES AND SCHEDULE OF ASSESSMENTS
Screening (Day -28 to Day -1): informed consent, medical history, physical
exam, ECOG, vital signs, 12-lead ECG, echocardiogram, complete blood count,
comprehensive metabolic panel, coagulation panel, pregnancy test, HIV/HBV/HCV
serology, bone marrow biopsy, PET/CT imaging, tumor biopsy for central
pathology review and biomarker analysis, pharmacogenomic blood sample
(optional sub-study).

Treatment period: 21-day cycles for up to 12 cycles. Study drug administered
by IV infusion on Days 1, 8, and 15 of each cycle with mandatory 4-hour
post-infusion monitoring for cytokine release syndrome (CRS) during Cycle 1.
Pre-medication with corticosteroids, antihistamines, and antipyretics required.
Hospitalization is required for the first 48 hours after the initial dose for
CRS monitoring.

Pharmacokinetic sampling: intensive PK draws at pre-dose, 0.5h, 1h, 2h, 4h,
8h, 24h, 48h, and 72h post-infusion during Cycle 1 Day 1, plus trough samples
at every subsequent visit.

Biomarker/specimen collection: mandatory tumor biopsies at baseline and Cycle
3; optional research biopsies at progression; whole blood for
immunophenotyping at every cycle; archival tissue submission required for
central lab confirmation of CD20 expression before randomization.

Patient-reported outcomes: FACT-Lym and EQ-5D-5L questionnaires administered
electronically at each visit via a dedicated ePRO tablet device provided to
each patient.

Long-term follow-up: patients will be followed for survival every 12 weeks
for up to 5 years after end of treatment, including telephone contact and
local lab review.

6. STATISTICAL CONSIDERATIONS
Sample size of 240 patients (160 active / 80 placebo) provides 90% power to
detect a 20% improvement in ORR at a two-sided alpha of 0.05, accounting for
a 10% dropout rate. Interim analysis for futility and safety planned after 80
patients complete Cycle 3, reviewed by an independent Data Safety Monitoring
Board (DSMB).

7. SAFETY REPORTING
Adverse events graded per CTCAE v5.0. Serious adverse events (SAEs) must be
reported to the sponsor within 24 hours of awareness. CRS and neurotoxicity
events must be reported using ASTCT consensus grading and reported to the
DSMB within 24 hours regardless of seriousness.

8. REGULATORY AND ANCILLARY REQUIREMENTS
Central IRB review required at all sites. Investigational New Drug (IND)
application on file with FDA. Sites must maintain a temperature-monitored
-20C freezer for biospecimen storage. Pharmacy must prepare study drug under
a validated aseptic compounding protocol with same-day administration only.
Radiology imaging must be submitted to a central imaging core lab for blinded
independent central review (BICR).
